speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) in the past three years, what is the percentage of successful appeals for earlier withdrawal of payouts by CPF members who had to retire early; (b) what are the main reasons for disallowing the appeals; and (c) whether the Ministry will consider another option for CPF Life payments that start payouts at the minimum retirement age.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Those with savings above the applicable Full Retirement Sum can withdraw all the monies above that amount.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Those who own a property may also withdraw their savings above the Basic Retirement Sum using property charge or pledge.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Under the Medical Grounds Scheme, CPF members may apply to withdraw or start their payouts before the CPF Payout Eligibility Age of 65.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The eligibility criteria include being permanently incapacitated, terminally ill, or having a severely impaired life expectancy due to illness.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Such applications have to be accompanied by the relevant doctors’ certification.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The remaining 35% were not successful because applicants did not meet the eligibility conditions.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Unsuccessful applicants were referred to other avenues of help, such as Workforce Singapore (WSG) and the Social Service Offices.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The unemployment rate for the same age group has remained consistently below 3% in the past five years.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: A contributing factor is the introduction of re-employment legislation in 2012, which made it an obligation for employers to offer eligible employees continued employment after the age of 62, up to the age of 65.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Re-employment has made it possible for many Singaporeans to work beyond the age of 62.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In 2017, the re-employment age was raised further from 65 to 67.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Medical Grounds Scheme will also continue to be available to eligible members who may need to withdraw or start their payouts earlier than age 65.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I am not asking the Minister to lower the payout age to 62.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The majority are okay with the payout age of 65.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But from time to time, there are residents who approach me.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: They are retired at 62, there are no "medical grounds" justification, they are healthy.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, they are asking whether CPF Board will consider another option.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: For the majority, the payout age is 65, whereas some can get it earlier.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: They are prepared to get a lower sum but at the retirement age of 62.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If I heard the Member correctly, it is to make the payout eligibility age lower for some people who want it, but maintain it at 65 for the rest.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The option has to be made available to all?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If you make early withdrawal an option for all, then, in effect, it is really a reduction of the payout eligibility age.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Today, the payout age can already be voluntarily deferred to 70 but the payout eligibility age remains at 65.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That is the earliest that the person can withdraw.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, the substance of the Member's request is really not an option but a reduction.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I hope I have correctly understood the Member's suggestion.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Yes, it is true that, currently, for those who want to extend and withdraw their money later, it is available as an option.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: It is only for those who have money who can afford to opt to withdraw their CPF money at a later age.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: But there are some who do not have money and they would like to withdraw earlier.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: So, we can have: Option 1, withdraw at 62 years and at much lower sum; Option 2, the current one, where withdrawal of the money is at age 65; Option 3, withdrawal of the money at 70 years old.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Among the 35 Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) countries, well over half have pension withdrawal age at 65 or above.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In fact, the highest today, as far as I know, is 67.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In light of increasing longevity, people living longer and the likelihood of them working longer, some countries have already set in motion the raising of the pension withdrawal age.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the case of Denmark, it will go up, if I recall correctly, from 65 to 67 in 2022.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the case of Germany, it will go up to 67 by 2031.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Against such a backdrop, we must really ask if it is wise to lower our own payout eligibility age for all.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There will be no option, it will have to be for all, especially considering how we now have re-employment legislation that puts an obligation on the employers to offer work up to 67.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: My sense is also consistent with what the Member said earlier that most workers understand this.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the last few months since we started the tripartite workgroup on older workers, I have met many union leaders.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: At the National Trades Union Congress' (NTUC's) suggestion, we did this in clusters – aerospace, logistics, healthcare, financial services and even the public sector – a very diverse group of workers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The CPF payout eligibility age did not come up very much at all.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: What has been said very clearly is that the workers want the opportunity to work longer.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is also consistent with the focus group discussions that we held with members of the public.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They want to keep working and save more.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I hear these workers and I understand them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I want to be able to help make it happen.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: At the same time, the employers have also expressed their concerns to me.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They have worries about their increased obligations and their considerations.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think we must not also dismiss lightly.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And this tripartite consensus concerns the retirement age which is currently 62, the re-employment age up to 67 today.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In this process, we take reference from what we have always done in the past, which is that the workers express their views, the employers express their views, and we try to find a common ground for the best way forward.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That is how we did it with the re-employment age of up to 65 and then, subsequently, to 67.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If we can have a good new tripartite consensus on the retirement age and the re-employment age, it will point the way forward for all of us that is helpful.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I ask for some time to get this done.
